name: 2021-2029 Housing Element Public Workshop
agenda_text:
City of La Habra Heights
2021-2029 Housing Element
  Public Workshop
  January 25, 2022
   Overview

• City land use authority granted to cities by the
  State with limitations
• Purpose: “Health, Safety & General Welfare”
• State Planning and Zoning Law
  (Government Code 65000 et seq.)

• Authority + responsibilities
   Overview

• Housing Element has been a required part of the
  General Plan since 1969

• Housing Element updates required every 8 years

• 2021-2029 update required by State law

• All elements of the General Plan must be consistent
  (e.g., Housing and Land Use)
   Housing Element
  Guiding Principles

• Maintain & improve existing housing
• Plan for regional growth needs for all
  economic segments & housing types
• Minimize constraints to housing of all
  types
• Affirmatively further fair housing
   Key Requirements

Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA)
  Adequate sites to accommodate assigned need

Housing for Persons with Special Needs
  Regulations & procedures consistent with fair housing law
   RHNA

• Mandated by State law & prepared by SCAG
• Each city must accommodate its assigned share of
  the region’s new housing need
• Housing for all economic segments
• Linked to available sites with appropriate zoning
   RHNA

6th Planning Cycle (2021-2029)
SCAG region:  1,341,827 units
Los Angeles County:  812,060 units
La Habra Heights:  172 units
  +72 units (5th cycle)
  244 units total
   RHNA

La Habra Heights (2021-2029)
Income
Category  Units
Very low  110
Low  54
Moderate  52
Above mod  28
Total  244
   RHNA

• RHNA is planning target, not a construction quota
• Inventory of sites must accommodate the RHNA,
  with focus on lower-income need
• Lower-income need can be accommodated
  through zoning for:
   Multi-family apartments & condos (20+ units/acre)
   Accessory dwelling units (ADUs)
   Special Needs

Persons with special needs
  Elderly
  Large families (6+)
  Persons with disabilities
  Homeless
  Female-headed households
  Farmworkers
   Special Needs

Zoning for persons with special needs
  Senior housing
  Residential care facilities
  Emergency shelters & navigation centers
  Transitional & supportive housing
  SROs
   Importance of
  Certification

• State Legislature has delegated authority to HCD to review
  Housing Elements for compliance (“certification”)

• Attorney General or other aggrieved party may file a
  lawsuit challenging the Housing Element

• Courts may impose fines, award attorney’s fees, order
  zoning changes and freeze building permits

• HCD certification supports the legal validity of the Housing
  Element and General Plan
   Draft Housing Element
I.  Introduction
II. Housing Needs Assessment
III. Constraints
IV. Resources & Opportunities
V. Housing Plan
Appendices
A. Public Participation Summary
B. Site Inventory

   Program Actions

Program H-2: General Plan & zoning amendments
   Multi-family zoning (12 acres)
   Allow lot clustering
   Reduced parking requirements
Program H-3: ADUs
Program H-4: Special Needs Housing
   Emergency shelters & navigation centers
   Transitional & supportive housing
   Employee housing
   SROs
   Residential care facilities
   Reasonable accommodation
   Density bonus for affordable housing
